svg.text: A Synchronological Chart of Bible and World History
4004 BC – AD 2030 · after Sebastian C. Adams, Synchronological Chart (1871) · open data: Theographic (CC BY-SA 4.0), STEPBible, Wikidata
Upper streams follow Ussher's chronology as Adams did (Jones/Theographic). Lower streams follow modern reign dates. Red connectors join the same event in both.

g.title: Ninety-five Theses · AD 1517 · Martin Luther, at Wittenberg

Diatessaron · c. AD 170 · Tatian's harmony of the four Gospels
Papyrus 46 · c. AD 200 · Paul's letters; dated about 175-225
Hexapla · c. AD 245 · Origen's six-column Old Testament: Hebrew beside the Greek versions
Codex Vaticanus · c. AD 325 · Copied about 300-325; one of the two oldest nearly complete Greek Bibles

Codex Alexandrinus · c. AD 425 · Copied about 400-440
Aleppo Codex · c. AD 930 · Pointed by Aaron ben Asher at Tiberias; much of the Torah was lost in 1947
Leningrad Codex · AD 1008 · Copied in Cairo in 1008 or 1009: the oldest complete Hebrew Bible, and the source of this project's Hebrew text (UXLC)
Wycliffe's Bible · c. AD 1382 · About 1382-1395: the first complete Bible in English, translated from the Latin
Gutenberg Bible · c. AD 1455 · The first major book printed with movable type in Europe
Novum Instrumentum omne · AD 1516 · Erasmus's Greek New Testament, the first to be published; the basis of the Textus Receptus
Tyndale Bible · AD 1526 · Tyndale's New Testament, the first printed in English and the first translated from the Greek
Luther Bible · AD 1534 · The complete German Bible; the New Testament appeared in 1522
Textus Receptus · AD 1633 · The name comes from the preface to the Elzevir edition of 1633
Tischendorf brings Codex Sinaiticus to light · AD 1859 · He found the first leaves at St Catherine's Monastery, Sinai, in 1844
